label: Close
description: End the exchange with the caller of this run, and say why. Behind a Socket it sends the close frame with `code` and `reason`. Behind a Route, `reason` is the response body under `status` (a String, sent the way Reply sends one), and with no reason it is a bodiless response (`status` defaults to 204; after a Stream only the end of the response is left). Close needs nothing from upstream to work, so the `_should_flow` gate is usually its whole wiring: prefill `reason` and `status`, then wire any output port of the branch that should end here into `_should_flow`, whatever that port's type (the value is never read, only a `false` says no). Every field takes a wire as well as a literal, so a `reason` a node computed can be wired in like any other input. The shape for "do this, and if it did not work, stop here" is a Switch on the outcome whose failing case gates this node and whose passing case gates the rest. A branch that skipped closes its ports, so the Close behind it skips too.

inputs.name: code
inputs.label: Close code (Socket, empty = 1000)
inputs.description: The WebSocket close code, Socket only: empty is 1000 (a normal closure), 4000 to 4999 are yours to define. Refused behind a Route.

inputs.name: reason
inputs.description: Why the exchange ended, a short sentence for the caller: the close frame's reason behind a Socket, the response body behind a Route (refused after a Stream, which already sent the response).

inputs.name: status
inputs.label: Status (Route, empty = 204, or 200 with a reason)
inputs.description: The HTTP status, Route only: empty is 204 with no reason and 200 with one; 204 with a reason is refused (a 204 carries no body). After a Stream the status already went out. Refused behind a Socket.

inputs.name: headers
inputs.label: Headers (Route)
inputs.description: Extra response headers by name (Route only), so an ending carries its own: a 304 with its `etag`, a 429 with its `retry-after`. A content-type here overrides the one a reason's shape implies. After a Stream they are refused (that head already went out), and refused behind a Socket.

outputs.name: done
outputs.description: Fires true once the exchange has been ended.

then.message: Close '{id}' answers nobody: no Route or Socket starts a run that reaches it. Wire it from the trigger's run (through data, or `_should_flow`), or put it in a group the trigger's `_should_flow` runs.
Close '{id}' has a `reason` and `status: 204`: a 204 carries no body, so the message would never reach the caller. Pick a status that carries one (400, 403, 404, 409...), or drop `reason`.
Close '{id}' sets `code`, the WebSocket close code, but a Route starts the run that reaches it. Say how it ended with `status` (and `reason`) instead.
Close '{id}' sets `status`, an HTTP status, but a Socket starts the run that reaches it. A close frame carries `code` and `reason` instead.
